title: Big Matlock introduces him to Louis's records
summary: In Omaha a Chicago musician played Louis records and introduced him to marijuana.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Now, I remember the first time I got turned on was Big Matlock [Big Matlock] turned me on, you know. And do you know how we met? In the music store. And everybody... Well, he was the first one that played the... First he had the play the record of Louis ...(?)..., and I can play the song to this day. We were in this music store in Omaha, Nebraska, with that show, that TOBA show there... He heard us humming the thing, and he said, "Are you guys musicians?" "Yeah." He said, "I'm from Chicago," and he asked if I'd heard Pops, and we didn't know anything about Pops, you know. He said, "Listen, you got anywhere to play any records?" I said, "No, but we can ...(?)..., me and my brother have a pad." He said, "Well, I'll come and get my box and bring some of those records, and let you hear him." So he went and he got his box, and we met him, and we went in these people's house...
So I'd seen him roll his own cigarettes, and I figured "Well, this guy is an important musician." So I said, "Man,

take one of my Luckies." He said, "No, I prefer this." "Damn, that smells strange!" Yeah! So he said, "Try it." In them days they called them Muggles. And I didn't know what the hell he was talking about. So we tried it. And I didn't pay much attention to it. But he played "Wild Man Blues", and those things stuck in my head -- I couldn't get them out of my head.
Well, that's as close as I came to getting to Louis before I came to New York. And that was in the early Twenties.
